note: NO FACT CHANGED. The kinds list is byte-identical to 0.11.0's and no fact type gained, lost or reshaped a member. This entry records a change to the INSTRUMENT: the closed-vocabulary scan attributed membership by shape, so a gate payload's vocabularies moved this fingerprint while nothing about facts did. Membership is now declared per vocabulary and a closure check asserts nobody forgot. Scoping it surfaced three vocabularies the old scan could not see because it required a list named `All`; one of them, Classifications, travels inside every change manifest, so this is also a real increase in coverage. Classifications is a ranking and is hashed in its own order - sorted, a reordering would change what may leave a customer's network and move no ledger. A reading taken by the corrected instrument cannot reproduce one taken by the broken one, which is why this bumps rather than matching 0.11.0.

note: NO KIND CHANGED - the list is byte-identical to 0.12.0's. What changed is a VALUE and two members. LoopMoves gains `write`, which is why this bumps at all: a member may be added freely and a value may not, because the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so an added value breaks every prior reader by design. Nothing in the vocabulary granted putting bytes at a path, so no flight could create a file - and `when: change.manifest touches migrations/**`, the gate this design is built around, most often fires on a new migration. Spelled `write` and not `create` because the tool overwrites and `create` would be a name true of one of its two uses; a new value rather than a widening of `edit`, because widening `edit` would change what an already-declared move permits for every envelope in force, retroactively, with nothing marking the day. environment.identity gains moveEnforcement and movesProbed - what this machine's executor bounds and what a startup probe proved withheld - with a new MoveEnforcements vocabulary behind the first. Not a boolean saying the bound held: the runner refuses to take work when it does not, so that member would be constant across every flight and record nothing. LoopBudget gains attempts, which is a member and costs nothing, and rides this bump rather than asking for one.

note: NO KIND CHANGED, and that is the finding rather than an omission - the list is byte-identical to 0.13.0's. An envelope change was the first candidate for a tenth kind and it is refused on the same argument that was already recorded once: a FACT is what crosses the boundary from a runner, and an envelope change has no runner and nothing crosses. A rejection reason was ruled out as a fact for exactly this reason in slice three - appending it would make the control plane pretend to be a runner and blur the one question the evidence model answers cleanly, which is who produced this - and decisions went into EvaluableFacts as a SOURCE instead, per ADR-0011. A proposal is the same shape in every respect that matters: control-plane origin, human author, an input to evaluation rather than an observation of a flight. What moves the fingerprint is a VALUE: ExecutorRungs gains `human`, and this vocabulary is fingerprinted here because a rung is what a loop.outcome fact reports having run. Existing envelopes are unchanged in meaning - none of them named it - and a reader meeting it for the first time halts rather than deciding which rung it is.

A flight that stopped may now have its work pushed so somebody on another machine can take it over, and that push opens no pull request - so a `gg/` branch with no proposal beside it is a real state for the first time. A reader counting this platform's branches has to be able to tell work that was admitted from work that was merely kept, and those mean opposite things about whether anybody is expected to review it. A MEMBER, so no prior reader halts, and null means what it always meant: a push on the ordinary landing path. What makes it move this ledger at all is that the fingerprint covers the shape of every registered fact type, not only the list of kinds - which is the whole reason the shape is in there. A member added to a fact a runner ships is a change to what the runner may say.

note: NO KIND CHANGED, AND NO MEMBER OF ONE. What moves is a CLASSIFICATION over the same nine kinds: FactCategories says whether each family describes a subject, the tree a flight touched, or the flight itself. It is in this ledger rather than the contract one because it is a statement ABOUT the fact vocabulary - the day somebody adds a family is exactly the day this table must move, and putting the two in one fingerprint makes adding and classifying a single reviewable act. ADR-0021 section 2. Two entries correct what slice sixteen shipped control-plane-side: destination.landed and destination.pushed were treated as needing a repository and are flight facts, because they measure what an EPISODE did rather than a standing property of a tree. And section 2's own table is corrected in the other direction - it names budget.attempts and check.verdict, neither of which is a fact family (one was never built, the other is deliberately absent with its reason recorded in Facts.cs), while omitting loop.transcript and handoff.account, which are. The classification is built from FactKinds.All rather than from the document describing it. Nothing a runner ships changes shape; a runner pinned to 0.16.0 produces byte-identical facts.

note: flight.nomination - the work kind a classifier nominates, and why - plus `propose`, the move that grants the channel it is declared through. TWO VALUES IN CLOSED VOCABULARIES, which is why this is a version move rather than an addition: the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so an added value breaks every prior reader by design. Envelopes in force are unchanged in meaning - they cannot nominate, which they could not before either. THE ONLY FACT AN AGENT DECLARES. Every other family is measured, from a tree or a session or a registry, and handoff.account is a person's own words. This one ASKS: that a flight of a particular work kind exist. It is stated by CONSTRUCTION rather than by a field, because EvidenceVoices is a member of GateEvidenceItem and of nothing else - there is no voice on a fact, and inventing one would be a new closed vocabulary with a gate behind it. What marks this as a claim is what marks a person's account as one: its own kind, its own envelope slot, and a name that says it is a nomination rather than a classification. A reader who could not tell them apart would read a request as a finding. AND IT DECIDES NOTHING. A work kind is not a label on a flight, it is the selection of a governance regime - the loop, the moves, the budget, the destinations and which obligations apply - so an agent able to name any of them would be choosing its own moves. The control plane holds the nomination against Destination.Opens, a menu a person wrote, and refuses anything outside it. The fact is the ask; admission is the answer. THE SHAPE IS A RATCHET AND THE PRESSURE RUNS ONE WAY. Every field somebody will want to add - a move the work needs, a scope, a budget, a destination, an approver - makes the nomination more useful and makes it configuration an agent writes. A reason able to name a move would be unreviewable policy arriving one sentence at a time. Two members, enumerated exactly rather than a list of bad names forbidden, because a forbidden-list passes on the third member nobody thought of. It names no flight and no parent either, which is where somebody would first add the reference ADR-0019 section 1 forbids. THE REASON'S BOUND IS MEASURED. A real classifier's reason for a clear-cut item ran about 700 characters, so 2000 is roughly three times what one needs; past it the agent is writing an analysis, and a fact carrying one belongs to the reference disposition rather than to a sentence somebody reads while deciding something. `PROPOSE` IS A MOVE RATHER THAN A NEW GATING MECHANISM, and that is what makes it cheap: the grant arrives through the --allowedTools list a launch already builds from LoopMoves, so the work kind never has to reach the runner. LeaseLoop carries four values and its own doc forbids more, because policy arriving at a runner is Article IX's failure wearing a convenience - keying the tool on the work kind would mean putting the work kind on the lease, which IS that failure. It is withholdable, unlike a tool for asking a person a question: that one must always be granted because an envelope able to withhold it would make a stuck agent silent, while this one is the whole output of one kind of work and a loop that is not classifying has no business nominating a kind. Record-only on MoveKinds' own criterion: the product is a fact, a destination still gates whether it becomes a flight, nothing leaves and nobody is messaged.

note: blocked - a fourth loop outcome, for an agent that asked for a decision it is not allowed to make and stopped. ONE VALUE IN A CLOSED VOCABULARY, which is why this is a version move rather than an edit: a reader built before it halts on meeting it, which is the closure working and the same trade ExhaustionPolicies.HandoffToAgent records. The fact KINDS are unchanged - nothing new crosses yet - and the surface moves because LoopOutcomes is part of it. WHY IT IS NOT DERIVED FROM THE RESULT RECORD, measured rather than assumed: four real runs against a ticket that could not be satisfied all reported subtype success and is_error false, having changed no file and said so. The one bit the executor chose on cannot tell an impasse from a completion, so the evidence is a tool the agent CHOSE to call - declared, never inferred, because a classifier reading repository content is injectable and a file in a customer's tree could make a flight declare itself blocked. It is not failed (a crash and an impasse need different people, the argument the vocabulary already makes about exhausted) and it is not completed (finished work and abandoned work need different people too). An agent that asked and then went on to change the tree stays completed, with the question recorded beside it: asking and finishing are two facts, not one state.

note: loop.question - an eleventh fact KIND, and it has to make the argument slice twelve's guard demands: a fact belongs to a flight and a routine action has none. A question belongs to the flight whose loop asked it, is produced by that loop, ships on that flight's lease and is keyed on that flight's id. It is not a flightless path grafted under the fact name. It is categorised FLIGHT rather than vetoed: it measures the episode, every work kind that runs a loop can produce one, and there is no subject that could rule out an agent asking a question. Bounded at 2000 characters and REFUSED rather than truncated - a question cut in half is one a person cannot answer, and one that arrives looking answerable is worse than one that was rejected, because the flight then waits on a gate nobody can close. Empty is refused at construction for the same reason one step further. Cleaned as PROSE, so its line breaks are its own: the field a person reads while deciding something is the wrong one to flatten.

note: loop.attended - a twelfth kind, plus AttendedGaps, a closed vocabulary of three. THE ONLY FACT WHOSE SUBJECT IS AN ABSENCE. Every other family reports something that was measured - a diff, a session, a registry, a person's own words, an agent's request. This one reports what a session could not see, because a person held the terminal and there was no stream to read. Categorised FLIGHT: it measures the episode, names no subject at all, and filing it under Tree would make it unproducible by the one kind of flight that produces it. A CLOSED VOCABULARY IS THE POINT RATHER THAN AN INCIDENTAL COST. The values are what a control plane halts on, and the only safe response to a gap a reader does not know is to stop: carrying it on would treat "something was not measured and I cannot tell you what" as handled. It is a SET rather than the kind's existence so that it can SHRINK - an executor that later measures moves for an attended session omits one value, where a derived declaration would freeze the gaps at whatever the first attended executor happened to be unable to see. Prior readers are unaffected in meaning: no runner ships this yet, and one pinned to 0.20.0 produces byte-identical facts. Cleaned as TIGHT throughout, unlike loop.question and handoff.account: nothing on this fact is written for a reader, so a line break in any of its values is a value captured with its own newline still attached rather than somebody's formatting.

note: AccountConfirmations gains `unaided` - an account written from nothing, because nothing was proposed. NO KIND CHANGED AND NO MEMBER OF ONE; the surface moves because AccountConfirmations is part of it. THE CONTRACT ALREADY NAMED THIS STATE AND HAD NO VALUE FOR IT. HumanAccount.WasProposed's own remark distinguishes "a replaced account had a proposal that was discarded" from "one written with no inference at all" - and the vocabulary carried accepted, edited and replaced, every one of them a relationship to a proposal, so the second could not be said. That is the week's recurring shape inverted: four separate findings were prose asserting a property the code did not have, and this is prose naming a STATE the code could not express. Same root either way - the description got ahead of the code and nothing compared them. `replaced` WAS THE TEMPTING ANSWER AND IT IS THE HARMFUL ONE, which is why the addition is worth a version rather than a reused value. Its own remark says it is "the signal that the feature is not working": the escape hatch for a proposal so bad it was easier to rewrite than to edit. A hand-flight has no proposal to be bad, so recording `replaced` for one would fire that signal on every hand-flight forever and make the inference look broken wherever it had simply never run. A quality measure that cannot tell "the proposal was rejected" from "there was no proposal" is not one. WHERE IT COMES FROM: a person handed a terminal by `gg fly --hand` writes what they did in the return file, and nothing proposed anything to them, because HandSession runs on the takeover path and not that one. Their words are the only account an attended flight has and the most informative thing in its record - loop.attended declares turns, moves and the tool bound all unmeasured, so what the machine knows about such a flight is mostly what it could not see. WasProposed stays NULL for these rather than false: how much of the proposal survived is not a question about an account that had none, and false would say a proposal was made and kept nothing of it. A reader built before this value halts on meeting it, which is the closure working and the same trade every other closed-vocabulary addition records.

note: AttendedGaps gains `transcript` - which file holds the conversation, and an attended session cannot say. NO KIND CHANGED AND NO MEMBER OF ONE; the surface moves because AttendedGaps is part of it, the same shape 0.24.0 records one value over. THIS ONE WAS ASSERTED IN A COMMENT AND IMPLEMENTED NOWHERE. AttendedTranscriptTests says a reader "learns that from the declaration on loop.attended" - and the vocabulary held turns, moves and move-bound, while AttendedExecutor mentions the transcript nowhere at all. So the absence was learned exactly the way the rule beside it forbids: from an empty fetch. That is the week's recurring shape for the fifth time, and the reason to keep counting it is that every instance was found by trying to PROVE a criterion rather than by anything failing. IT IS A GAP RATHER THAN A MEMBER OF ITS OWN, because that is what the other three are: a value a reader would otherwise infer wrongly. A missing loop.transcript means two different things on a platform where facts arrive in batches - one worth waiting for and one that will never come - and only the flight's own record can tell them apart. A dedicated member would need a vocabulary of its own and a validation arm for one value that never varies on this path. AND IT CAN NEVER BECOME A REFERENCE, which is why declaring the gap is the whole answer rather than a stopgap. The session file is at ~/.claude/projects/<mangled cwd>/<session_id>.jsonl; the id arrives in the stream-json init event, which an interactive session does not produce, so an attended executor cannot learn it - and one flight's tree directory was observed holding TWO files, with the directory outliving the tree that is swept. The newest is a guess, and a guess attributed to a flight is worse than an absence. Measured with a real agent on a real host, which is the only way that could be settled. A reader built before this value halts on meeting it, which is the closure working and the same trade every other closed-vocabulary addition records.

note: LoopMoves gains `propose-work-item` - an agent may say what a tracker should hold. NO KIND CHANGED AND NO MEMBER OF ONE; the surface moves because LoopMoves is part of it, the same shape 0.24.0 and 0.25.0 record one value over. IT IS A MOVE AND NOT A TOOL SETTING, because a move is the only thing an envelope declares that the runner turns into a granted tool: LoopMoves.All is what an envelope may name, ClaudeCodeExecutor.Tool is the single map from a named move to a qualified tool, and a tool with no move behind it is a tool nothing can ask for. Without this value the proposal tool would have to be granted unconditionally or named outside the envelope, and either one is a capability a governed flight holds that its own record does not declare. RECORD-ONLY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. MoveKinds classifies it beside `propose`: it writes a fact, the tracker is not touched, no agent holds a credential for one, and whether the fact becomes a write is a destination's answer. An agent that proposes has still not acted, so admission can refuse the whole batch and nothing outside the flight has moved. The kind is held in a dictionary rather than a switch precisely so a new move cannot arrive unclassified: the unclassified default would be record-only, and record-only is the answer that lets an unrecallable act be granted. A reader built before this value halts on meeting it, which is the closure working and the same trade every other closed-vocabulary addition records.

note: WorkItemOperations arrives - create, update, field, link, score - the menu a proposal names one of. NO KIND CHANGED AND NO MEMBER OF ONE; the surface moves because it is a closed vocabulary declared into the fact fingerprint, which is the fourth entry running with that shape and the FIRST that is a whole new vocabulary rather than a value on an existing one. IT IS DECLARED A STEP BEFORE THE FACT THAT CARRIES IT, deliberately and not by accident of ordering. The tool's schema is where a menu like this gets decided by default: an agent has to be offered the operations, and a list typed into the schema would have been a second spelling of something the extractor and admission both read. Two spellings of one menu make an operation proposable and unadmittable at the same time, which reads to everybody involved as a refusal nobody wrote. THE WHOLE GAMUT IS IN IT ON PURPOSE. A tool that offered `update` and withheld `create` would be refusing a proposal, and refusing proposals is admission's job against a menu a person wrote on the destination - so narrowing here would move a refusal from a place that records one to a place that leaves nothing behind. `field` is separate from `update` because a person admits them differently: rewording an item is nearly free to undo and moving it to another team's area path is somebody else's Monday, and a destination that wanted to permit one and not the other could not say so if both arrived under one name. `score` is separate from `field` because it is the one somebody asked for. VERBS FOR THE CHANGE, NOT FOR A TRACKER'S API: every tracker spells its writes differently and some have no notion of a link at all, so what is stable is what a person meant, and the adapter maps these onto whatever is in front of it. That seam is what lets a second tracker arrive without moving this. A reader built before this vocabulary halts on meeting a value from it, which is the closure working and the same trade every other closed-vocabulary addition records.

kinds: change.manifest, destination.landed, destination.pushed, environment.identity, flight.nomination, handoff.account, loop.attended, loop.digest, loop.outcome, loop.question, loop.transcript, source.provenance, work-item.proposal
note: work-item.proposal - A NEW KIND, the first since loop.attended and the thirteenth. Every entry since 0.22.0 moved the surface without moving the count, so this is the row those four were distinguishing themselves from. THE SECOND KIND THAT IS AN AGENT'S REQUEST rather than a measurement or an account, and the argument for a second is that it asks for a different thing: flight.nomination asks that a FLIGHT exist and this asks that somebody else's BACKLOG change. Both decide nothing - the control plane holds them against a menu a person wrote on the destination - and both are marked as asks the only way a fact can be, by their own kind and their own slot on FactEnvelope, because a fact has no voice field and a reader who could not tell an ask from a finding would read a request as a result. ONE FACT PER PROPOSAL AND THAT GRAIN IS THE POINT. A triage reads a backlog and proposes a dozen changes; each arrives as its own fact so each can be admitted or refused on its own. A fact carrying a list would make the batch the unit a person decides on, and 'yes to the re-field, no to the link' would have nowhere to be said. FOUR NAMED MEMBERS AND ONE THAT IS NOT, and the seam between them is the design. Operation, target, score and reason are named because a condition cannot be written over what it cannot see, and those are what a person says out loud when refusing one: not that operation, not on that item, not at that score. `detail` is a JsonElement nothing in the contract reads, because the questions somebody will ask of a score six months from now - which rubric, how confident, what was ruled out - are not knowable today, and a schema invented now would answer the wrong ones and silently discard the right ones. IT IS A FIELD RATHER THAN THE SHAPE: making the whole fact free-form would have been simpler and worse, because 'which part of this record is open-ended' would then be answered by knowing the history instead of by looking at where the opacity is declared. Structured rather than a string of JSON, so the later re-evaluation it exists for does not begin by parsing something twice. Its SIZE is bounded although its shape is not: the facts of one flight travel in one batch and unbounded means a repository can arrive in one. THE SCORE IS A STRING ON PURPOSE. P1, or 8, or 'high, 2 of 3 reporters blocked' - which of those it is belongs to the envelope and the skill, and an int here would settle it once for every rubric anybody writes later, in a place nobody consults while writing one. Classified under Flight in FactCategories, on flight.nomination's argument one subject over: a triage flight may take no repository at all because it reads a tracker, so filing it under Tree would make it unproducible by the only kind of flight that produces it, and every rule reading it structurally inapplicable for ever and silently.
